formation.title: The Middle Kingdom Reborn
formation.text:
For centuries, the lands between the Rhine and the Meuse have been the cockpit of Europe, fought over by France and the Empire, carved into duchies and prince-bishoprics, their unity a memory preserved only in the name 'Lotharingia.' Now that memory becomes reality once more. The kingdom that Lothair I carved from the heart of Charlemagne's empire at the Treaty of Verdun in 843 rises again.

But what manner of kingdom shall this be? The old Lotharingia was destroyed precisely because it tried to be everything, a corridor between rival powers, rich in trade and culture but lacking the military spine to defend its wealth. The new Lotharingia must choose its founding principle. Will it embrace its nature as Europe's crossroads, the land of the Champagne Fairs and the Rhineland fords, where tolerance and commerce create prosperity that makes conquest unnecessary? Or will it forge the iron discipline of the Burgundian ordonnance, building a centralized military state that secures its borders with fortresses and professional armies, demanding that the great powers acknowledge a third force in Western Europe?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the bridge between worlds. Let commerce and diplomacy be our strength.

modifiers.name: Crossroads of Christendom
modifiers.text: Lotharingia reclaims its ancient role as the meeting place of Europe, a land where merchants from the Rhine, the Meuse, and the Scheldt exchange not only goods but ideas, and where toleration of difference is not weakness but statecraft.

options.text: The Iron Crown of Lothar shall be defended by iron men.

modifiers.name: Iron Crown of Lothar
modifiers.text: The Middle Kingdom has risen again not as a passive buffer but as a martial state in the Burgundian tradition, its ordonnance companies and fortress-lined frontiers proclaiming that the space between France and Germany belongs to neither, it belongs to Lotharingia.

advances.name: Carolingian Palatine Tradition
advances.text: The tradition of the Carolingian palatinate, royal chapel complexes that served as centers of administration, justice, and sacred learning across the Middle Kingdom.

advances.name: Rhine River Commerce
advances.text: The great Rhine artery carries goods from the Alps to the North Sea, and those who control its crossings command the wealth of Western Europe.

advances.name: Scara Cavalry Tradition
advances.text: The elite scara, Charlemagne's mounted guard corps organized into cunei of fifty riders, left a lasting tradition of heavy cavalry excellence in the lands of the Middle Kingdom.

advances.name: Prince-Bishopric Administration
advances.text: The great prince-bishoprics of Cologne, Liege, Trier, and Strasbourg wield both spiritual and temporal authority, their cathedral chapters serving as centers of learning and governance.

advances.name: Flemish Cloth Trade
advances.text: The textile towns of Flanders and Brabant (Ghent, Bruges, Ypres, Brussels) produce the finest wool cloth in Europe, their lakenhallen serving as both marketplace and quality control.

advances.name: Brabant Fair System
advances.text:
The great fairs of Brabant (Antwerp, Bergen op Zoom, and their satellites) have succeeded the Champagne Fairs as the meeting point of Northern and Southern European commerce.

Available in: Lakenhalle

advances.name: Walloon Ironworking
advances.text: The iron forges of the Meuse valley, from Namur to Liege, have smelted ore since Roman times. Walloon smiths are renowned across Europe for the quality of their metalwork.

advances.name: Meuse Valley Defense
advances.text: The Meuse river valley, Lotharingia's central spine, has been fortified since the Carolingian era, its garrisons trained to hold the crossings against invaders from both east and west.

advances.name: Urban Communes
advances.text: The burgher communes of the Low Countries and Rhineland have won extraordinary self-governing rights, their councils, militia obligations, and guild regulations creating islands of proto-democratic governance.

advances.name: Early Netherlandish Art
advances.text: The revolution in oil painting pioneered by Jan van Eyck and Rogier van der Weyden has made the Burgundian Netherlands the artistic center of Northern Europe, their luminous altarpieces and portraits prized by courts across Christendom.

advances.name: Ordonnance Companies
advances.text: The compagnies d'ordonnance, permanent professional military companies first organized by Charles the Bold in 1471, represent the first standing army in Western Europe since Rome.

event.title: The Ordonnance Reform
event.text:
Following the example of Charles the Bold's revolutionary military ordinances of 1471, Lotharingia establishes its own compagnies d'ordonnance, permanent companies of professional soldiers organized into lances of men-at-arms, archers, and mounted infantry. This is no feudal host dependent on the seasonal availability of noble vassals. These are salaried professionals who drill year-round, maintain their equipment at state expense, and answer to appointed captains rather than hereditary lords.

The ordinance demands strict discipline: regular mustering, standardized weapons, prohibited gambling and looting without orders. It is the foundation of a modern army, and a statement that Lotharingia will not rely on mercenaries or feudal obligation to defend its frontiers.

options.text: The ordonnance shall forge our army anew.

modifiers.name: Ordonnance Reform
modifiers.text: The professional ordonnance companies bring modern military discipline to Lotharingia's armies, with standardized equipment, regular pay, and year-round drilling.

advances.name: Bourse of Antwerp
advances.text: The Antwerp Bourse, established in the early sixteenth century, is the world's first purpose-built stock exchange, a covered marketplace where merchants trade not goods but financial instruments.

event.title: The Bourse of Antwerp
event.text:
The great exchange building on the Meir has become something the world has never seen before, a permanent marketplace not for goods, but for money itself. Here, bills of exchange from Venice and Augsburg are traded alongside Portuguese pepper futures and English wool bonds. The Antwerp Bourse has eclipsed the fading fairs of Champagne and Bruges, drawing merchants from across the known world to a single trading floor where fortunes are made and lost in a day.

Foreign factors, Portuguese, Spanish, English, German, Italian, have established permanent residences in the city. The population swells. The city's annual fairs, once held twice a year, now function continuously. Antwerp has become the commercial capital of the Western world, and its wealth flows into the coffers of the Lotharingian crown.

options.text: Let Antwerp's exchange set the price of the world's goods.

modifiers.name: Global Emporium
modifiers.text: The Antwerp Bourse has become the commercial heart of the Western world, where the prices of goods from four continents are set daily.

advances.name: Staple Rights
advances.text: The staple rights of Cologne and Bruges compel all goods passing through their markets to be offered for sale locally, creating immensely profitable bottlenecks that enrich Lotharingian merchants.

advances.name: Order of the Golden Fleece
advances.text: The most prestigious chivalric order in Christendom, founded in 1430 by Philip the Good, whose golden collar and ram's fleece pendant mark the supreme distinction of European nobility.

event.title: The Order of the Golden Fleece
event.text:
In a ceremony of extraordinary splendor, the knights of the Order of the Golden Fleece gather in their chapter, the most prestigious chivalric order in Christendom, founded by Philip the Good of Burgundy in 1430. Its membership is limited to the greatest nobles of the realm, bound by oath to defend the Catholic faith and uphold the honor of their sovereign.

The Order's golden collar and pendant of a ram's fleece have become the supreme mark of aristocratic distinction in Western Europe. Kings and emperors covet membership. Its chapters, held in the great churches of Bruges, Brussels, and Mechelen, are occasions of matchless pageantry, processions of heralds, tournaments of arms, and solemn masses that proclaim the magnificence of the Lotharingian court to all of Europe.

options.text: The Golden Fleece binds the noblest blood of Europe to our cause.

advances.name: Printing Press Heartland
advances.text: The Rhine corridor from Mainz to Cologne and beyond, the birthplace and fastest adopter of Gutenberg's movable type, has become the information highway of Europe.

event.title: The Printing Revolution
event.text:
When Johannes Gutenberg perfected his movable type press in Mainz around 1440, he could scarcely have imagined how quickly the technology would transform the Rhineland. Within decades, printing houses have sprouted in Cologne, Strasbourg, Basel, and Brussels. The great Rhine corridor, already Europe's busiest trade route, becomes the highway of ideas. Books that once took a monk years to copy can now be produced in hundreds of copies in weeks.

The impact on literacy, religious debate, and the dissemination of knowledge is revolutionary. University cities along the Rhine attract scholars from across Europe. Legal codes are standardized and distributed. Commercial correspondence accelerates. The very concept of information has changed, and Lotharingia sits at the center of this transformation.

options.text: Knowledge shall flow as freely as the Rhine.

advances.name: Tapestry Workshops
advances.text:
The tapestry workshops of Arras, Tournai, and Brussels produce the most sought-after wall hangings in Europe, their monumental narrative scenes gracing the palaces of kings and popes.

Available in: Lakenhalle

advances.name: Confessional Balance
advances.text: In a land where Catholic, Reformed, and Lutheran communities live side by side, Lotharingia develops pragmatic traditions of religious coexistence that other realms will take centuries to discover.

advances.name: Walloon Guard Tradition
advances.text: The Walloon Guards, professional infantry recruited from the French-speaking provinces, serve as elite formations in armies across Europe, renowned for their steadiness under fire.

advances.name: Rhine Fortification
advances.text: The systematic fortification of the Rhine frontier with bastioned forts and star-shaped citadels, transforming the river from a trade route into an impregnable military barrier.

advances.name: Rhine Toll System
advances.text: The refinement of the Rhine toll system, from crude river chains and castle toll points to a rationalized customs service, turns Lotharingia's geography into a steady stream of revenue.

advances.name: University Tradition
advances.text: The universities of Leuven, Cologne, and Strasbourg form a corridor of learning that attracts scholars from across Europe, their faculties of law, medicine, and theology renowned throughout Christendom.

advances.name: Crossroads Diplomacy
advances.text: Lotharingia's position between France, the Empire, and the North Sea states makes it a natural broker of treaties and mediator of disputes, a role its diplomats exploit with skill.

advances.name: Centralized Customs
advances.text: The consolidation of Lotharingia's patchwork of local tolls, staple rights, and transit fees into a unified customs system, the foundation of a true internal market.

advances.name: Industrial Meuse
advances.text: The Meuse valley from Liege to Namur, rich in iron ore, water power, and centuries of metalworking tradition, becomes one of Europe's earliest industrial corridors.

advances.name: Fortress Builders
advances.text: Lotharingian military engineers, inheriting both the Burgundian and French fortification traditions, become masters of the bastioned trace italienne and the art of siege warfare.

advances.name: Commercial Code
advances.text: The codification of commercial law, drawing on centuries of fair regulations, guild statutes, and exchange practices, provides a stable legal framework for Lotharingia's merchants.

advances.name: Standing Army Reform
advances.text: The transformation of Lotharingia's military from a mix of provincial levies and mercenary companies into a centralized, uniformed, and professionally trained standing army.

advances.name: Coal and Steel
advances.text: The coal and iron deposits of the Meuse-Sambre basin fuel an industrial revolution that transforms Lotharingia from a land of artisan workshops into one of Europe's great manufacturing centers.

advances.name: Constitutional Assembly
advances.text: A constitutional assembly, drawing on Lotharingia's deep tradition of communal governance and estates assemblies, establishes a framework of codified rights and representative government.

advances.name: Modern Banking
advances.text: Building on centuries of exchange practice from the Antwerp Bourse to the Cologne merchant houses, Lotharingian banks pioneer modern financial instruments and credit systems.

advances.name: Lotharingian National Identity
advances.text: From the patchwork of Walloons, Flemish, Rhinelanders, Alsatians, and Lorrainers emerges a shared Lotharingian consciousness, not erasing local identities but weaving them into a common fabric.

advances.name: Citizen Army
advances.text: The levee en masse, universal military service drawn from all citizens regardless of estate, transforms Lotharingia's defense from a professional affair into a national obligation.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Middle Kingdom
destiny.text: With stability restored across the reconstituted Middle Kingdom, Lotharingia stands at a crossroads: will it become Europe's great commercial bridge, or forge an iron-willed military state?

event.title: The Foundation Holds
event.text:
The fragile miracle of reunification endures. Where skeptics predicted swift dissolution, the fate of every previous attempt to revive the Middle Kingdom, Lotharingia instead consolidates. The diverse peoples of the Rhine, the Meuse, and the Scheldt have found, if not unity, then at least a working arrangement. Walloon ironmasters and Flemish weavers, Rhenish vintners and Frisian fishermen, all discover that the Lotharingian crown offers something no neighboring power can: the freedom to trade and worship without the heavy hand of Paris or Vienna.

The question now is not whether the Middle Kingdom will survive, but what it will become.

options.text: The foundation is laid. Now we build.

destiny.name: The Rhine Entrepot
destiny.text: Secure Amsterdam for Lotharingia and ensure cloth flows through the capital markets. Build a treasury worthy of Europe's crossroads. Requires 1000 gold.

children.text: Cloth is produced in the market
Cloth is traded in the market

event.title: Amsterdam Secured
event.text:
The great port of Amsterdam, where the Amstel meets the IJ and a hundred ships crowd the harbor on any given day, now flies the Lotharingian standard. With Amsterdam's matchless commercial infrastructure and the cloth trade flowing through our capital markets, Lotharingia commands the economic crossroads of Northern Europe. The warehouses of the Warmoesstraat overflow with Baltic grain, English wool, and Mediterranean spices. Money-changers and factors from a dozen nations crowd the exchanges.

This is what the Middle Kingdom was always meant to be: not a fortress, but a marketplace, the place where Europe does business.

options.text: Amsterdam is the jewel in our commercial crown.

destiny.name: Banker to Europe
destiny.text: Raise houses of exchange in two of our towns, where the loans of kings are traded as at Antwerp, and accumulate the wealth that makes Lotharingia indispensable to every court in Christendom. Requires two Antwerp Bourses or merchants' quarters, 2000 gold and 50 prestige.

conditions.text: Has an Antwerp Bourse, Merchants Quarters, Grand Marketplace or Commerce Center in at least 2 locations

event.title: The Banks of the Middle Kingdom
event.text:
Lotharingian banking houses have achieved what no mercantile republic or royal treasury could: they have become indispensable. Kings borrow from Antwerp to wage their wars. Popes rely on Cologne factors to move their revenues. The bills of exchange issued in Brussels are honored from Lisbon to Danzig. The Lotharingian guilder, backed by the immense productive wealth of the Rhine corridor, has become the most trusted currency in European commerce.

But financial dominance brings its own dilemmas. Shall we use this leverage to reshape trade itself, opening markets and breaking monopolies? Or shall we invest our influence in diplomatic networks, binding the courts of Europe to Lotharingia through debt and obligation?

options.text: Open the markets. Free trade enriches all.

modifiers.name: Exchange Mastery
modifiers.text: Lotharingian exchanges set the terms of European trade, their bills of exchange and commodity futures underpinning the commerce of the continent.

options.text: Bind the courts of Europe to our exchange.

modifiers.name: Diplomatic Network
modifiers.text: A web of financial obligations and diplomatic ties binds the courts of Europe to Lotharingian interests, making our neutrality too valuable to violate.

destiny.name: Pax Lotharingica
destiny.text: Bring the great textile cities of Bruges and Ghent under Lotharingian sovereignty, and let Antwerp grow into what Bruges once was: the staple of the north, where the spice, the cloth and the silver of every nation change hands. Requires Antwerp at 66 development and 75 prestige. Unlocks the Handelshof building.

conditions.text: We own Antwerp and its development is at least 66

event.title: The Lotharingian Peace
event.text:
There is a phrase heard increasingly in the chanceries of Europe: 'Pax Lotharingica.' It refers not to conquest but to the remarkable stability that Lotharingian commercial networks have brought to Western Europe. When wars threaten trade, Lotharingian diplomats broker peace. When famine strikes a province, Lotharingian merchants redirect grain. The great textile cities of Bruges and Ghent, now under the Lotharingian crown, anchor a commercial network that stretches from the Baltic to the Mediterranean.

The Middle Kingdom has achieved what its founders dreamed: not dominion through arms, but indispensability through commerce. No power in Europe can afford to make war on the nation that holds the purse strings. Shall this peace be expressed through universal free trade, or through the cultivation of a cosmopolitan capital that draws the best minds of every nation?

options.text: Let the markets speak for themselves.

modifiers.name: Universal Market
modifiers.text: The Lotharingian commercial network has become truly global, its light ships carrying trade to every port while its markets recover swiftly from any disruption.

options.text: Make our capital the envy of every nation.

modifiers.name: Cosmopolitan Capital
modifiers.text: The great cities of the Middle Kingdom (Brussels, Antwerp, Cologne) draw scholars, artists, and merchants from every nation, creating a culture of tolerance and innovation.

destiny.name: The Burgundian March
destiny.text: Claim Dijon, the ancient Burgundian capital, and build an army worthy of Lothar's iron crown. Requires an army of 30 thousand men and 25 stability.

event.title: The March on Dijon
event.text:
The ancient capital of the Burgundian dukes falls to Lotharingian arms. In the great hall of the Ducal Palace, where Philip the Good once held his glittering court and Charles the Bold plotted his doomed ambitions, the Lotharingian standard now hangs beside the iron crown of Lothar. The message is unmistakable: Lotharingia claims not merely the Low Countries and the Rhineland, but the full inheritance of the Burgundian state, its military traditions, its chivalric prestige, and its territorial ambitions.

The Burgundian March has begun. The Middle Kingdom is no longer content to occupy the space between France and the Empire, it means to dominate it.

options.text: Dijon is ours. Let the great powers take notice.

destiny.name: The Middle Kingdom Restored
destiny.text: Extend Lotharingian sovereignty to Reims in the west and Hamburg in the north, establishing the frontier of a true middle European power. Requires an army of 50 thousand men.

event.title: The Frontiers Secured
event.text:
With Reims, the coronation city of French kings, under Lotharingian control in the west, and Hamburg, the great Hanseatic port, secured in the north, the Middle Kingdom has established frontiers that would have astounded Lothair I himself. This is no longer a narrow corridor between rival powers. It is a true continental state, commanding the Rhine from source to sea, the Meuse from headwaters to delta, and the overland routes from the Channel to the Baltic.

The question now is how to hold what has been won. Shall we build an impregnable line of modern fortresses along the frontier, making invasion suicidal? Or shall we revive the ordonnance tradition, investing in the tactical excellence of our field armies to meet any threat in open battle?

options.text: Build the fortresses. Make our frontiers impregnable.

modifiers.name: Fortress Line
modifiers.text: A continuous chain of modern fortifications along the Lotharingian frontier, supported by advanced logistics, makes invasion a suicidal proposition.

options.text: Drill the armies. Tactical excellence wins wars.

modifiers.name: Ordonnance Revival
modifiers.text: The revival of Burgundian ordonnance discipline produces field armies of exceptional tactical flexibility, though the concentration on land warfare leaves the navy neglected.

destiny.name: Hegemon of the West
destiny.text: Seize Paris, Frankfurt, and Mainz, the capitals of France and the Empire, proving that the Middle Kingdom is the greatest power in Western Europe. The crown that holds them is kept at Aachen, where Lothair's grandfather built his palace, and the palace town must be raised into a seat fit for it. Requires an army of 75 thousand men and Aachen at 62 development. Unlocks the Kaserne building.

conditions.text: We own Aachen and its development is at least 62

event.title: Hegemon of the West
event.text:
Paris has fallen. Frankfurt has fallen. Mainz has fallen. The three cities that anchor the power of France and the Holy Roman Empire, the political capital of the Capetians, the coronation city of the Emperors, and the seat of the premier Archbishop-Elector, all now answer to the iron crown of Lothar. The Middle Kingdom has not merely survived between the great powers; it has consumed them.

This is the Lotharingian century. From the Channel to the Alps, from the Atlantic to the Elbe, the territories of Charlemagne's empire are reunited under a single crown for the first time since the Treaty of Verdun. Shall this hegemony be expressed through an elite imperial guard that embodies centralized power? Or through the iron discipline of a professional army that fights for plunder as much as patriotism?

options.text: Forge an imperial guard worthy of our new dominion.

modifiers.name: Imperial Guard
modifiers.text: An elite imperial guard corps, equipped with the finest artillery and answering directly to the crown, embodies the centralized military power of the Lotharingian state.

options.text: Iron discipline and the spoils of war.

modifiers.name: Iron Discipline
modifiers.text: A professional army bound by iron discipline and incentivized by the systematic distribution of war spoils, supported by mercenary companies that supplement the standing forces.

units.name: Scara Cavalry
units.text: Elite heavy cavalry inheriting the tradition of Charlemagne's mounted guard corps, the scara, organized into cunei of fifty riders, trained in both shock charges and dismounted combat.

units.name: Meuse Border Garrison
units.text: Sturdy defensive infantry recruited from the Meuse valley fortifications, specialists in holding river crossings and fortified positions against superior numbers.

units.name: Ordonnance Lance
units.text: Professional heavy cavalry organized into the Burgundian lance formation, a man-at-arms accompanied by coutillier, page, and archers, drilled to fight as a coordinated unit.

units.name: Walloon Guards
units.text: Professional infantry recruited from the French-speaking provinces of Wallonia, serving as elite line troops renowned across Europe for their discipline and steadiness under fire.

units.name: Lotharingian Line Infantry
units.text: Uniformed professional infantry drilled in the linear tactics of the age, representing the culmination of Lotharingia's centuries-long evolution from feudal levies to a modern army.

units.name: Citizen Militia
units.text: Armed citizens mobilized through universal conscription, fighting with the fervor of free men defending their constitutional rights and national sovereignty.

buildings.name: Pfalzkapelle
buildings.text: A Carolingian palatine chapel complex modeled on Charlemagne's great chapel at Aachen, part royal chapel, part administrative center, part treasury, embodying the sacred authority of Lotharingian kingship.

buildings.name: Rheinzoll
buildings.text: A Rhine toll station positioned at a strategic river crossing, where customs officials inspect passing barges and collect the duties that fund the Lotharingian crown.

buildings.name: Lakenhalle
buildings.text: A monumental cloth hall where Flemish textiles are inspected, graded, and traded, both a market building and a statement of urban wealth and guild pride.

buildings.name: Walloon Forge
buildings.text: An iron forge in the Walloon tradition, using charcoal-fired blast techniques refined over centuries in the Meuse valley to produce iron of exceptional quality.

where.text: Iron is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Antwerp Bourse
buildings.text: The world's first purpose-built stock exchange, a columned trading floor where bills of exchange, commodity futures, and government bonds change hands in continuous commerce.

buildings.name: Rhine Fortress
buildings.text: A bastioned fortress commanding a Rhine crossing, its star-shaped trace italienne design incorporating the latest in military engineering to withstand artillery bombardment.

buildings.name: Meuse Ironworks
buildings.text: A large-scale ironworks in the Meuse corridor, using water-powered bellows and early blast furnace technology to produce iron on an industrial scale.

where.text: The location's raw material is Iron

buildings.name: Coal and Steel Works
buildings.text: A modern industrial plant combining coal-fired coke smelting with advanced steel production techniques, transforming raw ore into the structural material of the modern age.

children.text: The location's raw material is Iron
The location's raw material is Coal

buildings.name: Handelshof
buildings.text: A grand commercial court where merchants from across Europe gather to settle disputes, negotiate contracts, and trade under the protection of Lotharingian commercial law, the institutional embodiment of the Pax Lotharingica.

buildings.name: Kaserne
buildings.text: Professional military barracks housing Lotharingia's standing army, permanent quarters with armories, drill yards, and supply depots that keep soldiers combat-ready year-round.

list.name: Missi Dominici
list.text: Royal envoys, one cleric and one layman, sent in pairs on circuits called missatica to inspect counts, bishops, abbots, and the king's own agents. The institution was enlarged by Charlemagne's Capitulare missorum generale of 802 and was the central instrument by which Aachen reached into distant counties. Missi heard appeals, audited fiscal estates, promulgated capitularies, and reported back to the palace.

list.name: Aachen Palatine Chapel
list.text: The octagonal chapel built by Odo of Metz at Charlemagne's command and consecrated by Pope Leo III in 805, the architectural and liturgical heart of the Carolingian palace. The chapel housed the imperial throne, the royal relic collection, and the chapel-clergy who served as the king's notaries and intimate counsellors. Every coronation of a German king from Otto I in 936 to Ferdinand I in 1531 was performed beneath its mosaics.

list.name: Reichskirche
list.text: The imperial church system codified by Otto I after 962. The crown endowed bishoprics and royal abbeys with comital rights, market regalia, and immunities, and reserved the right to invest each new bishop with ring and staff. Because celibate prelates could not found dynasties, their offices reverted to the crown on death, a structural counterweight to the territorial dukes that anchored Ottonian and Salian government until the Concordat of Worms in 1122.

list.name: Kirchenvogtei
list.text: The lay-advocacy office that bound a magnate to defend a monastery or cathedral chapter in arms, hold its courts of blood-justice, and lead its men-at-arms to the Heerbann. From the tenth century the office became hereditary in noble families, who increasingly used the Vogtei as a vehicle to extract dues, depose abbots, and seize church property. The struggle over the great Lotharingian abbeys (Stavelot, Echternach, Prüm, Sankt Maximin) defined the politics of the Middle Kingdom.

list.name: Imperial Chancery
list.text: The writing-office attached to the palace and headed (after about 825) by an archchaplain who controlled the seal and supervised the notaries who drafted capitularies, diplomas, and royal correspondence. Under Louis the Pious and Lothair I, the chancery at Aachen produced the legislative texts that bound the realm into a single legal community. In the Ottonian centuries the archchancellorship became attached by custom to the archbishop of Mainz for Germany and to the archbishop of Cologne for Italy.

list.name: Treuga Dei
list.text: The Truce of God, introduced into Germany at the synod convened by Bishop Henry of Liège in 1082 and extended to the whole empire by the synod of Mainz in 1085 in the presence of Henry IV. The Truce forbade private warfare from sundown Wednesday to sunrise Monday, on church feasts, and during Lent and Advent; the Pax Dei added immunity from violence for unarmed clergy, peasants at the plough, and merchants on the road. Bishops enforced it with diocesan tribunals and the threat of excommunication.

list.name: Sauf-Conduit des Foires
list.text: The safe-conduct of the fairs. Beginning with Count Thibaut II of Champagne and confirmed by Philip Augustus in 1209, kings and lords swore to take under their personal protection every merchant travelling to or from the great cycle of six fairs at Lagny, Bar-sur-Aube, Provins, and Troyes. Lotharingian princes inherited and extended the practice across the Meuse, the Rhine corridor, and ultimately the Brabantine fair circuit at Antwerp and Bergen op Zoom, enforced by the merchants' own court of the Lex mercatoria.
